summary: Defines a MIB with managed objects for the Fibre Channel Fabric Shortest Path First routing protocol. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: This is a set of gauges for the route-picking system inside a storage network.

questions: fibre channel shortest path first snmp
what is a link state record in fspf
subtitle: SNMP objects for watching and tuning the routing protocol inside a Fibre Channel storage fabric.

tldr.problem: Fibre Channel switches route frames with the Fabric Shortest Path First (FSPF) protocol, but operators had no standard way to read its state or adjust its settings over SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4626 defines the T11-FC-FSPF-MIB module, with tables for per-fabric settings, per-interface settings and counters, the link-state database, and one notification for neighbor state changes.
tldr.outcome: A standards-track MIB that lets any SNMP manager monitor FSPF and configure some of its parameters. The RFC says it does not change FSPF itself, which FC-SW-4 specifies.

today: RFC 4626 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC. It remains the definition of the T11-FC-FSPF-MIB module.

sections.title: What This MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 4626 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managed objects related to the Fibre Channel Fabric Shortest Path First (FSPF) routing protocol. FSPF itself is specified in FC-SW-4, not in this RFC. The MIB module is written in SMIv2 and its objects are generally accessed through SNMP.

The module provides the means for monitoring the operation of, and configuring some parameters of, one or more instances of FSPF. It only holds information specific to FSPF. Information that would still apply if another routing protocol were used is placed in a separate MIB module, and this module extends the Fibre Channel Management MIB (RFC 4044).
sections.eli5: FSPF is the rulebook switches use to pick routes. This RFC does not change the rulebook. It only adds windows so people can look at how the rules are working.

sections.title: Fibre Channel and FSPF in Brief
sections.content:
A Fibre Channel Fabric is a switching network that connects end points called N_Ports. A switch port connected to another switch port over an Inter-Switch Link (ISL) is called an E_Port. Frames carry 24-bit address identifiers, and the Domain_ID is the highest level of the address hierarchy.

FSPF is a link-state path selection protocol. It tracks the state of the links on all switches in the Fabric and gives each link a cost. It computes paths by adding link costs and choosing the cheapest. The collection of link states is the topology database. FSPF has four parts: a Hello protocol, a replicated topology database, a path computation algorithm (for example Dijkstra's), and a routing table update.

The RFC also notes that FC-SW-4 adds Virtual Fabrics, where frames are tagged to show which Virtual Fabric they travel on. FSPF operates identically inside one.
sections.eli5: Switches are like road junctions. Each road has a price, and every junction keeps a map of all the prices so it can send data along the cheapest route.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Organized
sections.content:
Every table is indexed by three things: fcmInstanceIndex (a Fibre Channel management instance), fcmSwitchIndex (a switch managed by that instance), and a Fabric Index of type T11FabricIndex. A device on a single physical Fabric without Virtual Fabrics always uses a Fabric Index of 1.

The module is registered as mib-2 143. It has four groups:

  • t11FspfGeneralGroup: per-Fabric state and parameters.
  • t11FspfIfGroup: per-interface state and parameters.
  • t11FspfDatabaseGroup: the topology database.
  • t11FspfNotificationGroup: notifications for asynchronous FSPF events.

A separate counter group, t11FspfIfCounterGroup, holds the packet counters. Compliance requires it only for systems that count such events.
sections.eli5: Everything is filed by three labels: which manager, which switch, which fabric. Then it is sorted into four drawers: fabric settings, port settings, the map, and alarms.

sections.title: Fabric and Interface Settings
sections.content:
The t11FspfTable holds per-Fabric parameters and statistics. The agent creates and removes its entries as (Virtual) Fabrics are created and deleted. It includes t11FspfMinLsArrival (default 1000 milliseconds), t11FspfMinLsInterval (default 5000 milliseconds), the read-only t11FspfLsRefreshTime (30 minutes) and t11FspfMaxAge (60 minutes). Counters track path computations, checksum errors and LSRs discarded because they reached maximum age. t11FspfAdminStatus turns FSPF on or off for a Fabric; when it is disabled, FSPF provides no routes to the T11-FC-ROUTE-MIB (RFC 4625).

The t11FspfIfTable covers each interface. Per-interface timers are the Hello interval (default 20 seconds), the dead interval (default 80 seconds, which must be greater than the Hello interval) and the retransmit interval (default 5 seconds). The Hello interval must be the same at both ends of a link. Counters record Hello, Link State Update (LSU) and Link State Acknowledgement (LSA) packets in and out, retransmitted LSUs, and invalid control packets.

t11FspfIfLinkCostFactor (default 100) steers the choice of links through the formula Link Cost = S * (1.0625e12 / ifSpeed), where S is the object's value divided by 100.
sections.eli5: Each road has a timer for how often to say hello to the neighbor, and a price tag that depends on how fast the road is. You can read these and, for some, change them.

sections.title: The Topology Database and Notification
sections.content:
The t11FspfLsrTable is the database of the latest incarnations of Link State Records (LSRs) held for each Fabric. It is indexed by the owner's Domain Id and the LSR type, and it reports the age, the incarnation number, the checksum and the number of links. The most recent LSR is the one with the largest incarnation number. The t11FspfLinkTable lists the Inter-Switch Links inside each LSR, with the neighbor Domain Id, the source and destination E_Port indexes, the link type and the link cost.

Each interface also reports its neighbor state through t11FspfIfNbrState, using the six values shown below. The notification t11FspfNbrStateChangNotify fires when the neighbor state changes to a terminal state, either by regression (Full to Init or Down) or by progression (any state to Full). It is controlled by t11FspfNbrStateChangNotifyEnable, which defaults to false.
sections.eli5: The map shows every road and its price, and each map entry has a version number so switches know which copy is newest. An alarm can ring when a neighbor goes away or comes back.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several objects are read-write or read-create, and the RFC warns that SET operations in a non-secure environment can harm network operations. It lists what each group of writable objects can do: the timers alter how responsive FSPF is, the admin status objects enable or disable dynamic routing, the set-to-default objects can nullify valid configuration changes, and the link cost factor alters the choice of links.

The readable tables, including the LSR and link tables, may also be sensitive. SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security, so the RFC RECOMMENDS SNMPv3 with its cryptographic mechanisms and says deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators must make sure only legitimate principals can GET or SET these objects.
sections.eli5: Some of these dials can slow or break the network if the wrong person turns them. So the RFC says to use the secure version of SNMP and lock the dials down.
